Adobe today announced the launch of a beta version of the AI Assisted Editor, a new optional editing mode in Photoshop that uses a simplified prompt interface for image editing. Below is an overview of the new features in this release.

Photoshop introduces an optional AI Assisted Editor

Adobe announced the launch of the AI Assisted Editor, a brand-new beta experience that will replace Photoshop's traditionally detailed and complex image editing tools, switching to a prompt interface and simplified menus.

Users can find the AI Assisted Editor via a new toggle switch in the Photoshop menu bar, and can also hide it in settings at any time.

After entering AI Assisted mode, users will see a simplified interface that includes the following tools:

AI Assisted Editor includes:

Prompt to Edit: Transform images using natural language prompts, without the need for complex manual editing. Remove Background: Remove backgrounds, clean up edges, and customise images in just a few clicks. Generative Expand: Extend image dimensions and generate content that blends naturally into the composition. Remove Tool: Eliminate unwanted objects and distracting elements while preserving image realism. Generative Fill: Add, replace, or remove content with simple text prompts. Generative Upscale: Increase image resolution while maintaining sharpness and visual quality. AI Markup: Mark up images to visually communicate editing instructions for more precise results.

For first-time image editing users, or experienced users who need to work with rough concepts and quickly sketch out changes, the markup tool is particularly useful. Users can draw marks or click anywhere on the image, then add natural language instructions such as "add more clouds," "change these shoes," or "add a banner that says 'On Sale'" in English.

Adobe Firefly will make the adjustments, and users can continue fine-tuning the results in AI Assisted Editor mode, or switch back to the traditional pro editor for further modifications.

Other details announced today

In addition to the brand-new optional AI Assisted Editor beta, Photoshop has also added prompt-based masking editing, allowing users to roughly select the area of an image they want edited using Firefly Image 5.

Adobe said this feature responds to criticism of many existing prompt-based editors, as current versions sometimes degrade image quality or produce results that don't quite match the overall lighting or subject angle.

Photoshop today also launched another new feature: non-destructive layer tools for adjusting lighting, including adjustments for exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, white point, and black point. Adobe said: "Users can achieve Camera Raw-level results in the Photoshop layer workflow, without leaving Photoshop."

A new tool that's the complete opposite of the mask-based editing tool is "Prompt to Edit," which lets users modify an entire image with just one prompt, rather than editing only one part.

For example, users might want to turn a daytime photo into a night scene, or change a rainy photo to a sunny one—this tool can help.

This new tool supports FLUX 2 pro, FLUX Context Pro, Gemini 3.1 (paired with Nano Banana 2), Gemini 3 (paired with Nano Banana Pro), Gemini 2.5 (paired with Nano Banana), GPT Image 2, and Adobe's own models, and will create a new layer containing two edited versions.

Finally, Adobe also announced two new features designed to give users "more control, less distraction":

Dynamic Text, Shapes and Paths extends Photoshop's dynamic text capabilities to any custom shape or path, allowing text to automatically adjust along curves and freeform layouts while retaining original formatting without manual adjustments. Stock Panel Integration brings over 900 million Adobe Stock assets directly into Photoshop as a dockable panel, making it easy for users to find, preview, and use assets in their workflow.

The AI Assisted Editor launches today in beta, while the other tools are available to all users starting today.
